rows.claim: Under a common skewed driver, static third-order co-skewness alone predicts the cognition target.
rows.scope: synthetic 4-node model with a single common skewed driver spread via a shared lag-1..3 HRF-like kernel; Ridge(alpha=1.0), 5-fold CV

rows.claim: Co-skewness adds essentially nothing over a directed / multi-lag FC baseline: its incremental predictive power collapses to ~0.
rows.evidence: common_source.incr_over_poor mean -0.0007 (std 0.0018); common_source.incr_over_rich mean -0.0011 (std 0.0018) — both within noise of zero and slightly negative
rows.scope: synthetic common-driver regime; few-lag (poor) and 6-lag VAR-style (rich) directed baselines

rows.claim: Co-skewness retains only a small increment over a static LINEAR FC baseline (the increment that a directed baseline then absorbs).
rows.evidence: common_source.incr_over_static mean 0.0265 (std 0.0125): small positive over static FC, vanishing once directed lags are modelled
rows.scope: synthetic common-driver regime; static linear FC baseline only

rows.claim: The effect requires a shared skewed source: without a common driver, co-skewness carries no cognition prediction.
rows.evidence: independent_source.coskew_alone mean -0.031 (std 0.016); independent_source.incr_over_poor mean -0.0089 — at or below chance with no common driver
rows.scope: synthetic null regime (same marginal skew, no common driver)

rows.claim: A common skewed driver plus HRF-like lags is SUFFICIENT to produce cognition-predictive static co-skewness that a directed-FC baseline absorbs.
rows.evidence: the full common_source pattern: coskew predictive alone (0.478) but ~0 increment over directed FC (-0.0007/-0.0011), absent in the no-common-driver control
rows.scope: synthetic sufficiency demonstration only; not a necessity or real-data claim

rows.claim: Real fMRI/HCP co-skewness IS this identifiability artifact (the necessity / real-data version of the thesis).
rows.evidence: not tested — synthetic generative model only; no real BOLD data, no real directed/VAR baseline, no temporal/phase-shuffle test on data
rows.scope: would require a directed/VAR baseline and a temporal-shuffle control on the paper's actual subjects (e.g. HCP); not run

rows.claim: The residual increment of co-skewness over a richer directed baseline on real data is negligible.
rows.evidence: reported small but run-to-run unstable in the duel transcript; not resolved by this compute
rows.scope: transcript discussion only; no stable real-data measurement
